hook.text: Bulk sequencing averages millions of cells — single-cell sequencing reads each cell's genome or transcriptome individually.

buildup.text: Droplet-based methods encapsulate individual cells with barcoded beads — each cell gets a unique molecular tag.

discovery.text: The Human Cell Atlas aims to map every cell type in the body — single-cell RNA sequencing reveals cell identity.

twist.text: Tumors are mosaics — single-cell sequencing reveals resistant clones hiding within a seemingly uniform cancer.

climax.text: Spatial transcriptomics maps gene expression to tissue location — seeing which genes are active where in a tissue section.

punchline.text: Every cell tells a different story — single-cell sequencing listens to each one.

quiz.question: Why is single-cell sequencing important for cancer treatment?
options: It makes chemotherapy more effective by increasing drug concentration
It reveals resistant clones hiding within a tumor that bulk sequencing would miss
It eliminates the need for tumor biopsies

details.summary: Single-cell sequencing analyzes DNA or RNA from individual cells rather than tissue averages, revealing cellular diversity within tumors, organs, and developing embryos. It has uncovered previously unknown cell types, rare cell populations, and cell-to-cell variation invisible to bulk methods.
details.whyItMatters: Bulk sequencing averages signals across millions of cells, masking the diversity that drives biological function and disease. Single-cell resolution reveals which specific cells drive tumors, immune responses, and development, enabling far more
takeaways: Individual cell analysis reveals diversity hidden by bulk tissue averaging
Single-cell RNA sequencing has identified thousands of previously unknown cell types
Cancer heterogeneity at single-cell resolution explains treatment resistance

faq.question: How does single-cell sequencing work technically?
faq.answer: Tissue is dissociated into individual cells. Microfluidic devices or well plates capture single cells with unique barcoded primers. Each cell's RNA is reverse transcribed with its barcode, pooled, and sequenced.

faq.question: What has single-cell sequencing revealed about cancer?
faq.answer: It shows tumors contain diverse subpopulations with different drug sensitivities. Rare resistant clones present before treatment expand after therapy. The tumor microenvironment contains immune cell subtypes with opposing pro- and anti-tumor functions.
